extracted.intended_audience: Developers contributing code and documentation to the SageMath codebase
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing Sage library code, docstrings, LaTeX in docstrings, and doctests so that examples are readable, testable, and consistent across the Sage documentation and codebase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and respect differing style preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge different authors may have different preferences on stylistic matters and respect the style choice of the author who first wrote the code or the docstrings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are different opinions and instances of different styles in the codebase; to prevent disputes, accept variation and respect original author's choices rather than holding votes to change local style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private function naming and docstring policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions whose names start with an underscore are considered private. They do not appear in the reference manual, and their docstring should not contain any information that is crucial for Sage users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private function docstrings may be made part of another method's documentation (e.g. via automethod links). Private functions should contain an EXAMPLES (or TESTS) block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructor (__init__) docstring behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The __init__ docstring is used as the class docstring if there is not one already.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can rely on the constructor docstring to serve as the class docstring; examples in the guide show how sage_getdoc returns the constructor docstring as the class docstring.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX usage in docstrings
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX code is allowed in Sage’s documentation and is marked with backticks. For LaTeX commands containing backslashes, either use double backslashes or begin the docstring with a raw string r""".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer r""" (raw string) for LaTeX backslashes (recommended). E.g. use r"""Return \sin(x)\""" or raw string so single backslashes work as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MATH blocks for displayed mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: MATH block syntax (.. MATH::) is similar to LaTeX \[ ... \] or $$...$$ and is used for displayed math in docstrings and rst files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building PDFs, each MATH block is wrapped automatically (e.g. in \begin{gather}..\end{gather}). If using LaTeX environments like align which shouldn't be wrapped, add a :nowrap: flag to the MATH block. See Sphinx math documentation for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability balance for LaTeX in interactive console
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interactive console, LaTeX formulas are represented by their LaTeX code (backslashes stripped), which may be less readable for some users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make formulas pleasant for interactive users when possible — e.g. prefer a/b or a b^{-1} instead of \frac{a}{b} when that increases readability in the console.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local LaTeX macros for common rings/fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Typeset standard rings and fields using locally-defined macros (e.g. \Bold{Z}) and use provided shortcuts \ZZ, \RR, \CC, \QQ, \GF{q}, \Zmod{p}, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These appear as LaTeX-formatted macros in html and as plain symbols in interactive help; see SAGE_ROOT/src/sage/misc/latex_macros.py for full list and instructions to add macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctests serve as both examples and tests; they must pass
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples in documentation both illustrate usage and act as tests checked before each release. All new doctests added to Sage should pass all tests (sage -t your_file.py should produce no errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctests help avoid regressions; follow the testing guidance in Running Sage’s Doctests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctests should show interesting examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctests should include interesting examples of what the function can do; these are most helpful to users and can include demonstrations of famous theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples should illustrate typical and instructive usage; include outputs/comments to aid understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test all meaningful combinations of input arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctests should cover all meaningful combinations of input arguments (e.g. different values for an algorithm parameter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a function accepts algorithm='A' or 'B', include doctests demonstrating both to ensure implementations and interfaces are exercised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check corner cases in doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctests must check corner cases (e.g. 0 input, empty set, null matrix, null function) as these are likely to break.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corner-case checks probably belong to the TESTS block; ensure these cases are covered in doctests to prevent regressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test interruption behavior for long-running functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a function might take a very long time, use ensure_interruptible_after() to check that the user can interrupt it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: use ensure_interruptible_after(1) and then sleep(3) to test interruption after 1 second.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic tests for small inputs or random instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctests should include systematic tests of all small-sized inputs, or tests of random instances when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TestSuites may help generate some of these tests automatically (see sage_unittest.py). For random tests, use tags or checks that don't depend on a specific random outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest environment: copy/pasteability and imports
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctests should work if you copy/paste them into Sage’s interactive console — include necessary imports when the function is not available by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show 'from sage.all import *' or explicit imports; ensure examples are runnable as-is in a typical Sage interactive session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking doctest blocks and variable scope
rubrics_metrics.description: All blocks within the same docstring are linked: variables set in one doctest keep their values for remaining doctests within the same docstring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use different variable names for unrelated examples to make data flow clearer and to help doctester's data flow analysis; use .. link to connect verbatim blocks across an rst file or .. linkall for whole-file linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage preparsing behaviour in doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctest input is preparsed like in the standard Sage shell: for example, 4/3 returns 4/3 (a Sage rational) rather than 1.3333 as in Python.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of preparsing when writing expected outputs and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use temporary files/directories in doctests writing files
rubrics_metrics.description: If a test outputs to a file, the file should be a temporary file; use tmp_filename() or tmp_dir() helpers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write permanent files during doctests; use provided helper functions to avoid leaving artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiline doctests: use continuation marker
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiline doctests should use the line continuation marker '....:' for subsequent lines of input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the interactive prompt where continuation lines start with '....:'. Use this pattern both for examples and in doctested code snippets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrap long doctest lines to fit documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrap long doctest lines so that readers do not have to scroll horizontally; aim around 80–88 columns and never exceed 95 columns in the source file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If breaking an expression not already nested, wrap it in parentheses. Do not wrap strings. Import statements need not be wrapped. If output is inherently wide, show a smaller example first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting long output for readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrap and indent long doctest output to maximize readability in source and HTML output, but maintain fidelity (do not alter string contents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no whitespace where you could wrap, do not insert whitespace just to wrap lines; keep output faithful to actual representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest tag alignment and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctest tags for modularization purposes (such as # needs sage.modules) should be aligned at column 88 to reduce visual clutter; tags that must be visible without scrolling (e.g. # optional - pynormaliz) should be aligned to be readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctest fixer uses tab stops; choose alignment so the important part of the tag remains visible in HTML at reasonable window widths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Split long lines following Python rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When splitting long lines inside doctests, use standard Python line-splitting rules (parentheses, continuation markers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show splitting arithmetic expressions across continuation lines. Keep resulting code valid and consistent with Python formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest magic comment: random
rubrics_metrics.description: The '# random' magic comment marks that the line will be executed but its output will not be checked against the documentation output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when output is nondeterministic (e.g. hash or random output). Prefer to avoid '# random' by testing properties rather than concrete random outputs when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest magic comment: long time
rubrics_metrics.description: The '# long time' tag marks lines that are only tested if the --long option is given; use for doctests that take more than a second. No example should take more than about 30 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this tag for expensive tests and provide reasonable expectations on runtime; example shows '# long time (1 second)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest magic comment: tolerance (tol)
rubrics_metrics.description: The '# tol' or '# tolerance' comment causes numerical outputs to be verified only up to the given absolute or relative tolerance; can be prefixed by abs[olute] or rel[ative].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of abs/rel is specified, zero expected value uses absolute error, nonzero uses relative. When multiple numerical values appear (complex numbers, matrices), each number is checked individually. The doctesting framework uses float_regex to identify numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest magic comment: not implemented / not tested
rubrics_metrics.description: The '# not implemented' or '# not tested' tag marks a line that is never tested, useful for long illustrative examples or todo notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clearly communicates to readers that the example does not currently work; use sparingly for documentation of intended behavior or placeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skip doctests for file/directory (nodoctest)
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of the first 10 lines of a file starts with nodoctest (in various allowed forms) the file will be skipped; if a directory contains nodoctest.py then that directory is skipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files or directories explicitly given on the command line are always tested. If adding such a line, add a note to module-level documentation explaining why doctests are skipped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional/needs tags for conditional doctest execution
rubrics_metrics.description: A line tagged with 'optional - FEATURE' or 'needs FEATURE' is tested only if the feature is available in Sage. If FEATURE starts with '!', the condition is negated. The --optional flag can force testing irrespective of availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for optional packages, features, internet access, known bugs, or modularization. Words after '# optional'/'# needs' are interpreted as package/feature names. Tags are case-insensitive; punctuation ends the package list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect doctest tag
rubrics_metrics.description: Use '# indirect doctest' in a function A's docstring when the example calls A indirectly (A is tested but not explicitly named), preventing coverage reports from showing the docstring as untested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for testing special methods like __repr__, __add__, or when A is exercised by calling another function B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture-specific output flags (32-bit / 64-bit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use '# 32-bit' or '# 64-bit' tags for tests that behave differently on 32-bit vs 64-bit machines. Apply these flags to the output lines, not the input lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per coding style, magic comments should be separated by at least two spaces; for multiline doctests place the comment on the first physical line of the doctest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and formatting of doctest magic comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Magic comments should be formatted consistently: separated by at least two spaces from code, with block-scoped tags placed immediately after the prompt to apply to the block, and for multiline doctests the comment on the first physical line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comments apply at intended scope and are visible in formatted outputs; this improves readability and doctest fixer behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use search_src to find doctest tags and todo items
rubrics_metrics.description: Use search_src or grep to find occurrences of tags like '# optional', '# not implemented', '# needs', etc., to discover tests to fix or features to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searching for 'todo: not implemented' can guide further development by locating placeholders and known incomplete tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running automated doctests: syntax and correct Sage installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Run sage -t <file> to test examples in .py, .pyx, .sage, .rst files. Use the ./sage from the SAGE_ROOT of the installation you are testing to avoid version mismatches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ./sage -t src/sage/games/sudoku.py. Using a system-wide sage or different version can cause import failures and false negatives; cd to SAGE_ROOT and use the local ./sage executable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing reST documentation and linking verbatim blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sage -t <filename.rst> to test verbatim environments in reST files. Use '.. link::' to link verbatim environments so variables persist, or '.. linkall' to link all; '.. skip' before a verbatim environment skips that example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See tutorial files for examples of including automated testing in reST documentation and for how to structure linked/verbatim blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: General coding style regarding whitespace
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spaces instead of tabs for indentation (except makefiles where tabs are syntactic). Do not add trailing whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sage provides editor configuration for Emacs (.dir-locals.el) to use spaces; configure other editors similarly to avoid tabs and trailing whitespace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-ASCII names in identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate non-ASCII letters in identifiers for consistency: translate ä and ö to ae and oe (e.g. moebius_function), and á to a (e.g. lovasz_number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these transliteration conventions when naming functions or identifiers to avoid encoding issues and to maintain consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common function keyword arguments should be standardized
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard keyword arguments with specified meanings for consistency: algorithm, certificate, proof, check, coerce, inplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meanings and defaults: algorithm (string or None) selects implementation; certificate (bool, default False) returns (result, certificate or None); proof (bool, default True) requires proven computation; check (bool) performs extra parameter checks; coerce (bool) converts inputs to suitable parent; inplace (bool) modifies object in-place or returns copy. Do not use different keyword names with the same meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctester recognizes sage: prompts and performs preparsing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sage doctesting framework is based on Python's doctest but recognizes sage: prompts and preparses input as in interactive Sage sessions. It supports parallel testing, timeouts, optional tests, and other Sage-specific features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the doctester features (parallel testing, timeouts, optional tests) and the sage -t command with flags like --long or --optional when appropriate; ensure examples conform to Sage interactive behaviour.
